title: The release gate passes a stale committed platform binary: compare a build or probe behaviour, not a checksum map against itself (DEC-204)
description:
DEC-204 (OPAG-1419), filed from the DEC-161 AC4 verification at dev b337381d on 2026-10-19. QCLI-438 is the HANDOFF RECORD for this defect, not the fix; this task is the fix. Publishing stays the operator (DEC-151).

DEFECT. The release gate (scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs) hashes each committed platform binary and compares the digest ONLY against a checksum map (manifest.questBinarySha256 and rootPackage.questPlatformPackages[...]) that is regenerated from those same committed binaries. The map therefore always agrees with the binaries, and nothing rebuilds from the current src/ and compares. A binary stale relative to src/ passes by construction.

MEASURED AT dev b337381d. The committed npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest blob f5702eb7 (sha256 59d1c0dc...) contains no --fields string. It answers `task view <id> --fields title` and `task list --fields id` with exit 2 (Unrecognized flag), while the same commands exit 0 from src/cli/main.ts at that SHA. The installed quest 0.13.0 binary is byte-identical to that committed blob, so published 0.13.0 lacks QCLI-312 and QCLI-291. QCLI-438 records the same class for QCLI-437: five of six committed binaries embed the pre-fix help string "--source <project>" while src/ has zero occurrences.

RULING (DEC-204). Replace the self-referential comparison with build-then-compare, or with a behavioural probe. For 0.14.0 the probe is: on the committed host-platform binary, `task view <id> --fields title` and `task list --fields id` must exit 0; the 0.13.0 binary must exit 2 on the same commands as the negative control in the same run. The fix must be proven both ways: a deliberately stale binary goes red, and a fresh build goes green.

SCOPE. Gate fix only; no release and no publish. QCLI-499 (release 0.14.0, quest half of the pair with lore-cli#572) is made a dependency of this task so the pair stays blocked behind it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A deliberately stale committed binary fails the release gate in a run that also passes a binary freshly built from the same source tree, so the gate is proven in both directions

For 0.14.0, the committed host-platform binary answers `quest task view <id> --fields title` and `quest task list --fields id` with exit 0, while the 0.13.0 binary exits 2 on the same commands as the negative control in the same run (behavioural-probe route), or the build-then-compare route demonstrates the identical stale-versus-fresh difference by building and comparing both
The gate no longer passes a binary solely because its digest matches a checksum map generated from that same committed binary, and the route chosen is recorded in the task final summary
QCLI-499 records a dependency on this task, so the 0.14.0 pair release is blocked until the gate is fixed

plan: 1. Add scripts/release-binary-probe.mjs: probe the committed host-platform binary with `task list --fields id` and `task view <id> --fields title`, asserting exit 0 and the projected shape; release-context enablement predicate.
2. Wire the probe into scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs so the release gate refuses a binary that cannot answer the probes, while leaving source-gates green in the strings-first bump state.
3. Tests: injected stale (exit 2) versus fresh (exit 0) results prove the gate red and green in one run; no-probe-ran fails; enablement predicate.
4. Real both-ways proof: committed host binary (stale) fails, freshly compiled host binary passes, same run; record exit codes.
5. Update the release runbook and CHANGELOG; run bun run check under pinned 1.4.2 and lore check.
6. PR, CI green, dispatch-check, independent review, then hold before land.
implementationNotes: Execution note (DEC-204 relay, OPAG-1419): built on DeepSeek with a Stage 1 review; if the change touches CI workflows (DEC-182 floor), opum-doc does an Opus review by ref.

RUN AND ROUTE. opum-control run job-1rbehfg; dispatch 17:25:13Z exit 0; applied model claude-sonnet-5-5 under floor:release (the route label said deepseek). Pack: /Users/jdnewhouse/.local/state/opum-control/packs/db17766c3cad63c9424dc965263d9f37adb4a818cf2840920d7b8d1063812c3b.json (sha256 db17766c...).

BRANCH AND HEAD. fix/QCLI-509-release-gate-stale-binary, PR #624, pushed code head 2854f9a2452dc9dafd18d882594a33fbdd1bcb95; this note moves the head, so read the PR headRefOid for the SHA under review and for CI. Tree clean at handoff.

IMPLEMENTED. scripts/release-binary-probe.mjs (probe pair: task list --fields id and task view <id> --fields title, each in the DEC-204 spelling plus a --json shape arm; fails on a failed command, an empty or id-less listing, or an accepted-but-ignored projection), wired into scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs and release-scoped by releaseProbeEnablement (QUEST_QUALIFICATION_TARGET equals the host, or QUEST_RELEASE_BINARY_PROBE=1; never source-gates, because the strings-first bump state must stay green with still-stale binaries). Tests: test/qcli509-release-binary-probe.test.ts (7). Runbook and CHANGELOG updated. No .github/workflows file touched.

CRITERIA SO FAR. AC1 MET: the deliberately stale committed darwin-arm64 binary (sha256 59d1c0dc...) fails probe 1 with exit 2 while a fresh compile of this tree passes all 4 probes and reads QCLI-1, in the same run (exit 0). AC3 MET in implementation; the route must be recorded in the final summary at completion. AC4 MET: QCLI-499 records dependencies ["QCLI-509"] (release/0.13.1-prep commit 76f2a7d0). AC2 PARTIAL: the negative half is measured (0.13.0 binary exit 2); the positive half was measured on a fresh compile of this tree, because the committed binary is still 0.13.0 until the 0.14.0 rebuild. At completion, decide whether that evidence satisfies AC2 and state precisely which object was measured.

LOCAL CHECKS (pinned bun 1.4.2 at /opt/homebrew/Cellar/bun/1.4.2/bin). typecheck, lint, format:check, layer:check and test:mod all exit 0; full bun run test = 1215 pass, 0 fail; lore check exit 0 (the 4 pre-existing profile-capacity warnings); Tracker integrity mirrors pass (CLAUDE.md declares 0.13.0 = package.json, tracker reads cleanly, agents --check exit 0).

NEXT. Wait for CI on the pushed head; then (a) append the completion note and check the criteria, (b) complete QCLI-509 in this same PR before review, citing PR #624 and the run that validated the code commit (never the merge SHA), commit and push the tracker move, (c) wait for CI green on the final head, (d) run opum-control review dispatch-check job-1rbehfg --sha <head> --repo /Volumes/external/repos/quest-cli and act only on ok:true, (e) independent review with the opum-workflow:review-assignment Workflow per the job-006dilp precedent: inputs are the task, the full head SHA, the repo path, run job-1rbehfg, attempt "1" (a string), author quest-cli, local checks mirroring source-gates, Tracker integrity and lore check, base = the merge-base with origin/dev; write .result verbatim to a file and run opum-control review record job-1rbehfg --sha <full-sha> --review-result <file>; never hand-compose an envelope and never use --human-reviewer. At most two rounds, then one confirmatory delta check.

LEADER ADDITIONS. Hold before land and report the PR, head SHA, dispatch-check result, the verdict as recorded, and whether workflows were touched; run opum-control task land job-1rbehfg <pr> only on the leader word "land". DEC-182: if the diff touches .github/workflows, tell the leader BEFORE land and opum-doc does an Opus review by ref (this diff does not touch them). Publishing and the pair release stay the operator (DEC-151). Stop and report on any verb refusal, a non-pass after round 2, or anything needing design.

ALSO STILL TRUE. Local commit 0655769d on release/0.13.1-prep remains deliberately unpushed (local branch 1 ahead / 1 behind origin at 76f2a7d0); do NOT push, rebase, reset or discard it. lore-cli#572 keeps its QUEST_SOURCE_REF pin at 848c304f until cut time. QCLI-505, QCLI-506 and QCLI-507 stay held.

COMPLETION 2026-10-19 (run job-1rbehfg; renewed session). Everything below was re-measured in this session, not inherited from the handoff.

CI ON THE CODE HEAD. PR #624 head 92c293db5bc16f932e50804f79c4c69c253c7a1c (that head touches only .quest/tasks/QCLI-509.json, so source-gates fired once, from the pull_request trigger). Newest row per context: source-gates success (started 17:40:40Z, completed 17:45:09Z), Tracker integrity success, lore check success.

BOTH WAYS, ONE RUN, A REAL COMPILE. The committed npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest reports --version 0.13.0 and FAILS probe 1: `task list --fields id` exit 2, "Unrecognized flag --fields" (ok:false, probesRun 1). A binary compiled in this session from this tree (`bun build --compile --target=bun-darwin-arm64`, pinned bun 1.4.2, output to the session scratchpad and never into npm/) PASSES all four probes and reads task QCLI-1 (ok:true, probesRun 4). Both were probed by scripts/release-binary-probe.mjs in one process. An interpreted `bun src/cli/main.ts` run gives the same fresh result.

THE GATE ITSELF, BOTH WAYS. `QUEST_RELEASE_BINARY_PROBE=1 bun run check:packages` exits 1 with "The committed darwin-arm64 binary does not implement capabilities this source tree has" plus the probe problem. The same command with the variable unset exits 0 and prints "darwin-arm64: release binary probe skipped (not the native qualification job for darwin-arm64 (QUEST_QUALIFICATION_TARGET=unset))". That skip is the release scoping that keeps source-gates green in the strings-first bump state.

THE ENFORCEMENT PATH IS LIVE WITH NO WORKFLOW EDIT. immutable-candidates sets QUEST_QUALIFICATION_TARGET from its matrix (.github/workflows/prepublication-qualification.yml:154), runs scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs, which runs `bun run check:packages` (prepublish.mjs:340), which now calls the probe. On a tag ref build:packages is skipped, so there the probe executes the COMMITTED bytes, which are the artifacts being published.

CRITERIA. AC1 met: the stale committed binary fails while a freshly built binary from the same tree passes, in a single run, with both objects named above. AC2: the committed host-platform binary today IS the 0.13.0 one and it exits 2, so AC2's first clause ("the committed 0.14.0 binary answers ... exit 0") is not measurable until the 0.14.0 rebuild. Its second clause -- building and comparing both, demonstrating the identical stale-versus-fresh difference -- is exactly what the both-ways measurement shows, so AC2 is checked on that evidence with the object named: a binary COMPILED from this tree, not the committed one. The committed-0.14.0 clause is enforced by the gate at the rebuild rather than claimed here. AC3 met: the checksum map is no longer the only test, and the route chosen (behavioural probe, not build-then-compare) is named in the final summary. AC4 met, re-read from the ref rather than trusted: origin/release/0.13.1-prep commit 76f2a7d0 gives QCLI-499 dependencies ["QCLI-509"]; the LOCAL prep branch is one commit behind that, deliberately holding local note 0655769d.

No .github/workflows file is touched by this branch (the PR file list confirms it).

REVIEW ROUND 1 2026-10-19 (attempt 1, recorded seq 24479, verdict changes-requested). Three findings: two fixed in code and docs, one is a tracker judgement corrected here.

F1 (major, scripts/release-binary-probe.mjs:262) -- real, confirmed and fixed. envelopeData returns undefined when the --json view envelope carries no `data` key, while the view branch guarded both shape assertions with `record !== undefined`; a data-less envelope therefore passed the view half with ok:true. The list half already refused a non-array data. Fixed by treating an undefined record as a problem ("carried no data to project"). The new test 'a view envelope with no data key fails rather than passing on an unread record' pins it; the suite is 8 tests.

F2 (minor, runbook:292) -- fixed. "immutable-candidates ... executes the committed artifact as-is" is true only on a tag ref; a dispatched run rebuilds first. The runbook, the probe module header, the gate's error and success lines (which now name npm/quest-<target>/bin/<exe>) and the CHANGELOG now say which object they mean.

F3 (minor, this record) -- accepted. AC2's first clause names the committed 0.14.0 binary, which the rebuild produces and which does not exist yet; checking it on a binary compiled from source was one inference past the evidence. AC2 is now UNCHECKED with that reason stated. The both-ways evidence for the gate stands on its own under AC1. AC2 is verified at the 0.14.0 rebuild under QCLI-499, which the gate now enforces on the committed bytes.

The no-workflow-touch and AC4 claims are unchanged: PR #624 still touches no .github/workflows file, and origin/release/0.13.1-prep commit 76f2a7d0 still carries QCLI-499 dependencies ["QCLI-509"].

REVIEW ROUND 2 2026-10-19 (attempt 2, sha 419fd736, recorded seq 24541, verdict APPROVE). Three minor findings, all fixed; none blocking.

F1 -- the durable finalSummary carried stale counts (7 tests, 1215 pass) written before the round-1 test existed. The suite is 9 tests now (8 at the moment of round 2) and the full run reports 1216 pass, 0 fail. Corrected in the appended summary, with the figures taken from a real run.

F2 -- a --json view envelope whose `data` is null threw TypeError out of probeReleaseBinary instead of being reported. The round-1 guard covered only `undefined`, and `Object.keys(null)` then threw. Now `record === undefined || record === null`, and the test 'a null data field is the same read-nothing failure, not a thrown TypeError' pins it (suite 9). It failed closed before, so the gate was never bypassed.

F3 -- the gate's failure text concluded "so it is stale relative to src/" unconditionally; on a dispatched run the probed file was just rebuilt from src/, so a failure there means the build is broken rather than that the bytes are stale. Reworded to name both possibilities.

Round 2's own unresolved items, recorded so the next reader does not inherit them as settled: it did not re-measure a freshly COMPILED native binary passing (it verified the source interpreter's projected shapes and the committed binary's exit 2, and measured the gate end to end both ways), and it could not measure `task list` on a detached HEAD under its read-only assignment, offering code inspection instead. The compiled-binary pass was measured in this session before round 1: bun 1.4.2 `bun build --compile --target=bun-darwin-arm64`, all four probes, task QCLI-1, alongside the committed 0.13.0 binary failing probe 1 in the same process.
finalSummary:
Fixed the release gate's blind spot (QCLI-509 / DEC-204). check-package-artifacts.mjs validated each committed platform binary only against a checksum map regenerated from those same bytes, so a binary stale relative to src/ passed by construction. Added scripts/release-binary-probe.mjs, a behavioural capability floor that executes the committed host-platform binary and requires `task list --fields id` and `task view <id> --fields title` to exit 0 and return the projected shape (each with a --json arm that asserts the shape, and refusals on a failed command, an empty listing, or an accepted-but-ignored projection). It is wired into check-package-artifacts.mjs and release-scoped by releaseProbeEnablement: it runs in the native immutable-candidates job (QUEST_QUALIFICATION_TARGET equals the host target, which on a tag ref is the path that executes the committed artifact as-is) or under QUEST_RELEASE_BINARY_PROBE=1, and is skipped in source-gates so a strings-first version bump stays green while the binaries are still the previous bytes. ROUTE CHOSEN (AC3): the behavioural probe, not build-then-compare. Tests: test/qcli509-release-binary-probe.test.ts (7). Verified on 2026-10-19: typecheck, lint, format:check, layer:check and test:mod exit 0; full `bun run test` 1215 pass, 0 fail; lore check exit 0. Both-ways proof, one run: the committed 0.13.0 darwin-arm64 binary fails probe 1 with exit 2, while a binary compiled from this tree passes all four probes and reads task QCLI-1. Gate level: QUEST_RELEASE_BINARY_PROBE=1 makes `bun run check:packages` exit 1 on that stale binary, and the same command with the variable unset exits 0 reporting the probe skipped. CI green on PR #624 head 92c293db (source-gates, Tracker integrity, lore check). Runbook docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md and CHANGELOG updated.

Review round 1 (changes-requested, seq 24479): the view half of the probe accepted a data-less `--json` envelope, now fixed and pinned by a test (suite 8). The runbook, module header, gate messages and CHANGELOG now name which binary is executed and note that only a tag ref runs the committed bytes as-is. AC2 is left unchecked: its subject is the committed 0.14.0 binary, which the rebuild produces, so it is verified then rather than claimed now.

Correction after review round 2 (approve, seq 24541): the probe suite is now 9 tests and the full `bun run test` reports 1216 pass, 0 fail -- the earlier "7 tests / 1215 pass" figures predate the review-pinned tests. Two further minor findings fixed: a `data: null` view envelope is reported as a read-nothing problem instead of throwing, and the gate's failure text no longer asserts staleness on the path where the binary was just rebuilt.

Counts, measured after the round-2 fixes: the probe suite is 9 tests and the full `bun run test` reports 1217 pass, 0 fail. (Round 2 measured 1216 pass with 8 tests; the earlier "7 tests / 1215 pass" is the pre-review figure.) This line supersedes both earlier counts.
